migration.description: Extend the execution Session boundary with durable, owner-scoped creation intents that can exist before a real external thread and execution generation are confirmed.
migration.release_unit_description: Phase-one execution-domain candidate following migration 00009; this migration is reserved for the Server-side Session creation and access boundary.

durable_state.description: Session creation command identity, immutable creation parameters and summary, creator identity, selected host, optional task target and unknown outcome survive process restarts before external side effects are reconciled. Confirmed Session rows retain their existing public shape.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL columns and indexes on execution_sessions managed by the embedded Goose migration history. Existing 00009 rows remain confirmed legacy records with nullable ownership facts and are never assigned an owner automatically.

source_compatibility_range.to_program_version: Phase-one Session creation-intent candidate containing migration 00010.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Apply the complete Session creation-intent schema unit, including nullable external identity, intent columns, row invariants and indexes, in one Goose transaction; there is no independent DML or historical backfill step.

progress_signals: A fresh PostgreSQL schema is migrated through 00009, a real 00009-shaped execution_sessions row is stored, and migration 00010 is re-entered after an actual index-collision failure; TestSessionIntentMigrationFrom00009 verifies rollback leaves version 10 unapplied and the pre-migration row unchanged before cleanup and successful re-entry.
A repeated DB.Migrate leaves the migration history and all four creation-intent indexes unchanged; TestSessionIntentMigrationReentry verifies re-entry on the deployed schema.
Existing 00009 rows remain confirmed legacy rows with nullable owner, host and command facts; TestCreationIntentLifecycleAndCompatibility verifies that no owner is inferred.
CreateIntent commits the creator-scoped command identity and creation payload before the caller performs a Gateway or Connector side effect.
Concurrent identical retries converge on one Session ID; a changed payload, summary, host or target under the same creator command identity returns an idempotency conflict.
Unknown intent state remains queryable and cannot be activated by a fresh identity; activation updates external thread, execution generation and any task binding in one transaction.
pause_points: The 00010 migration has no internal pause point: Goose commits or rolls back the complete schema unit atomically.
After the 00010 transaction commits and before the new application coordinator reads or writes creation intent rows.
After an intent commit and before the external Gateway or Connector call.
After an ambiguous external result is marked unknown and before reconciliation.

recovery.faulty_release_recovery: forward-repair-by-a-new-program-version; the stopped 00010 candidate is not repaired by assigning owners to old rows or by reusing an unknown command identity

required_test_evidence: The PostgreSQL migration path from a fresh 00009 schema to 00010 is exercised by TestSessionIntentMigrationFrom00009 with a real pre-stored 00009 execution_sessions row; the focused re-entry test confirms the complete index set after a second migration pass.

A deliberate collision inside the actual 00010 Goose migration rolls back the preceding ALTER statements and leaves version 10 unapplied; removing only the deliberate conflict permits the same migration to re-enter successfully, proving the deployed DDL unit is atomic.
Existing 00009 confirmed Create/Get records remain readable without public REST or protocol schema changes, and no historical owner, host or command value is inferred.
A same-command concurrent intent race commits one durable Session ID, while changed payload, summary, host and task target values conflict and same payload retries do not create another row.
Projectless intents retain the authenticated creator and selected host, and unknown intent state is queryable without an external thread reference.
Activation requires a real external thread reference and explicitly named execution generation, and atomically preserves the existing one-to-one task binding rule.
Host WSS generation and Worker generation are not accepted as Session execution generation fields; migration discovery is idempotent and no historical owner assignment occurs.
